nodes.title: Pi
nodes.subtitle: Agent interface and local tool dispatcher
nodes.description: The plugin registers Blackwall as the chat provider. Model calls and tool execution follow two separate server paths: chat uses /v1/chat/completions, and every tool_call uses /v1/tool-decisions. The plugin shows approval requests in its UI and starts a local tool only after consuming a grant.
nodes.input: User message, model response, tool result, or approval decision.
nodes.output: Model request, tool-decision request, local execution, or response to the user.
conditions: Missing configuration or unavailable Blackwall blocks the tool; the plugin does not choose a local default allow.

nodes.title: Blackwall
nodes.subtitle: Model proxy, policy Core, and tool gateway
nodes.description: The central server authenticates the session, checks model input and output, supervises text, decides tool requests, issues and consumes one-time grants, and records the audit. The model response is buffered and checked before it is returned to Pi; SSE is synthesized from the already-checked response. The Pi plugin reports start and completion through /v1/execution-events; Core does not run local tools.
nodes.input: Chat request, content for inspection, tool proposal, approval resolution, or administrator publication.
nodes.output: Checked upstream request, response to Pi, denial, approval request, or one-time execution grant.
conditions: A terminated, blocked, reviewing, or awaiting_approval session cannot proceed to the model or tools.
In observe mode, a soft denial may allow and execute an operation while recording observed_effect; hard denials and USER_REJECTED still block.

nodes.title: Agent model
nodes.subtitle: Provider and model selected by policy alias
nodes.description: Blackwall selects a provider/model from the alias, reserves budget, sends the prompt, and receives the complete response. The gateway supports OpenAI and Anthropic; the demo uses OpenAI. The response can contain text, a tool_call, or both. This is the agent-model role, separate from Guardian and Jev.
nodes.input: Prompt and tool definitions after gateway checks.
nodes.output: Buffered text or a proposed function/tool call.
conditions: Not called after an input, session-state, model-allowlist, prompt-size, or budget block.
Output text and tool_call arguments are checked by Blackwall before release.

nodes.title: Embeddings — OpenAI / vector cache
nodes.subtitle: Similarity → topic candidate; no verdict by itself
nodes.description: The embedding provider returns vectors for event text and catalog examples. Blackwall’s topic detector computes cosine similarity, applies thresholds, and selects candidates locally. A cache can reduce repeated OpenAI calls. A vector or similarity score alone is not evidence of a violation.
nodes.input: Redacted text from user_input, model_output, tool_arguments, tool_output, or model_input, plus topic-catalog examples.
nodes.output: Embedding vectors (from OpenAI or cache). Blackwall computes similarities, applies thresholds, and selects topic candidates.
conditions: Runs only when topic_supervision.enabled=true.
An embedding error or exhausted budget blocks the operation (fail-closed).
A topic assigned through users.*.topic_ids is a trusted label, not an embedding result.

nodes.title: Guardian
nodes.subtitle: Session-event supervisor; separate role from the agent model
nodes.description: When a session has an assigned topic or an active candidate, Guardian evaluates the current event against allowed and forbidden clauses, trusted policy, and limited history. The code makes a separate supervisor call; the configured provider can be OpenAI or Anthropic. A violation is enforced only when it includes a quote that is a substring of the event and a verified forbidden clause.
nodes.input: One current event, session history, assigned/candidate topics, and trusted policy clauses.
nodes.output: no_identified_violation, violation, or uncertain, plus candidate-label updates.
conditions: no_identified_violation → the event may proceed.
violation with evidence → the session is terminated.
uncertain or an unverifiable clause/evidence → the session enters reviewing; further tools are blocked.
Guardian error or an ungranted control budget → block.

nodes.title: Jev
nodes.subtitle: Semantic review of proposed operations, separate from Guardian
nodes.description: Jev compares the trusted user task with a specific proposed operation, verified facts, and policy context. It does not review every text event. Every allowed bash call is reviewed; other tools depend on profiles.*.semantic_evaluate. A Jev denial stops the proposal; an uncertain result may require approval if all reason codes are eligible.
nodes.input: Proposed tool and arguments, trusted task, deterministic-check facts, and policy context.
nodes.output: allow, deny, or uncertain with reason codes.
conditions: Called after session state, budget, tool allowlist, deterministic checks, secret/feed scan, and event supervision.
semantic_evaluate: all; mutating_and_outbound; shell_and_outbound; none. Bash is an exception and always goes to Jev.
Jev is not part of an embeddings → Jev chain; Guardian and Jev receive different inputs and answer different questions.

nodes.title: Active policy and catalog
nodes.subtitle: Shared configuration plane for every branch
nodes.description: The active policy, effective global/user scopes, profiles, topic catalog, topic policies, feed, and version govern the gateway, supervision, tool decisions, and executor settings. Runtime publication validates a candidate and uses PublicationGate to wait for active HTTP request leases; it does not wait for local Pi tools. A transaction stores the configuration, invalidates pending approvals and available grants, and swaps Core. A claimed and already-running Pi executor can continue.
nodes.input: Base configuration and authenticated publication with expected_version / expected_feed_version.
nodes.output: A new active policy and feed version used by subsequent checks in every session.
conditions: A stale version returns a conflict; invalid structure or semantic errors leave active configuration unchanged.
Publishing a topic catalog requires the complete topics + topic_policies pair.
An early denial may not include execution metadata; a later grant consume may then reject the request.
Publication invalidates grants in available state, not claimed grants; a local Pi executor already running may finish.

nodes.title: User approval or administrator review
nodes.subtitle: Two distinct human-resolution paths
nodes.description: A one-time operation approval is shown in the Pi interface. It is available only when approvals.enabled and every required reason code is in eligible_reason_codes. Separately, Guardian uncertain pauses the session in reviewing and creates a topic review for an administrator. User approval does not override a topic prohibition; the administrator chooses no_violation or violation and has no override option.
nodes.input: require_approval for an eligible operation, or a topic review after an uncertain result.
nodes.output: Approve/reject for one operation; separately, admin no_violation/violation for a review.
conditions: User approval is limited to one operation and expires; after approval, Core recalculates the decision.
Rejection, expiration, or publication while waiting prevents execution.
An administrator decision of violation terminates the session; no_violation resumes it.
If Pi has no UI, the plugin cannot ask for approval and blocks the operation without auto-approval.

nodes.title: Executor and one-time grant
nodes.subtitle: Deterministically checked, argument-bound, and consumed before start
nodes.description: Core creates a short-lived grant only after an allow decision. The plugin immediately sends consume with the same request/tool/arguments/cwd. Core checks session state, policy version, argument and directory hashes, repeats deterministic checks, and atomically claims the grant. Only then does Pi run the local file, shell, or HTTP executor; Core does not run the tool. The plugin inspects the result before showing it in the UI or adding it to model context.
nodes.input: Allowed decision, exact tool arguments, and working-directory context.
nodes.output: Locally executed result returned to the Pi plugin; disclosed only after inspection.
conditions: The grant is bound to the session, request, tool, arguments, working directory, resource hash, and policy version.
A mismatched, expired, previously consumed, or invalidated grant does not start the tool.
Files and HTTP use their own executors; a grant is not execution itself.
The native shell runs with the Pi process’s operating-system permissions; timeout and require_isolation do not provide operating-system isolation or a sandbox.

nodes.title: Audit and sessions
nodes.subtitle: Evidence of the run; not another decision model
nodes.description: SQLite stores session states, decisions, supervision results, approvals, execution grants, and publications. An audit event confirms a record or receipt, but an allow decision alone does not confirm execution start or completion; execution receipts are needed.
nodes.input: Core, gateway, executor, approval-resolution, and publication events.
nodes.output: History for the UI, later checks, and administrator review.
conditions: Sensitive content is redacted or omitted in demo views.
Publication preserves raw session history, but events cleared earlier do not authorize traffic under a new version.

scenarios.outcome: The full prompt structure, including system/developer and prior assistant messages, is scanned for secrets. Topic supervision reviews session events as they arrive, and the model response is inspected before release.

notes: Pi handles chat and tool execution through separate server gateways: model traffic goes through /v1/chat/completions, and every tool_call is checked independently before Pi starts the tool.

Embedding similarity creates a topic candidate; it is not itself a violation. Guardian supervises current session events only when a topic is assigned or an active candidate exists. Jev reviews proposed tool operations under separate routing rules.

Guardian and the agent model have different roles and are called separately. They may use the same model alias, although the demo uses a separate Guardian alias. The code supports OpenAI or Anthropic as Guardian provider.
The model response is buffered before inspection. If streaming was requested, the server sends synthetic SSE chunks only after checking the full response.

Runtime publication applies across paths: candidate validation and detector initialization happen before the active Core is swapped under PublicationGate. The transaction updates sessions, approvals, grants, and topic labels.

Main scenarios assume mode=enforce. In observe mode, a soft denial may allow and execute an operation while recording observed_effect; hard denials and USER_REJECTED remain blocking. Observe therefore affects execution, not just the audit.

The optional BLACKWALL_GATEWAY_TOOLS=1 path lets the gateway ask Core for decisions on model tool calls from clients without the plugin. It returns a decision only: it does not consume a grant or run a tool. Execution remains with the client. Pi uses its required path: decision, grant consumption, and local executor.

In Pi, the tool runs locally in the plugin after a successful grant consume. The plugin reports execution to Blackwall and inspects the result before showing it; the executor does not connect directly to Blackwall.
PublicationGate synchronizes server-side HTTP request leases, not local Pi execution. Publication invalidates available grants; a grant already claimed and an executor already running may finish.
The shell executor runs with the Pi process’s permissions. The require_isolation declaration and timeout do not create an operating-system sandbox.

Policies in the diagram mean a local configuration snapshot in Core memory, not an HTTP service. Authenticated administrators initiate publication through the API. OpenAI returns vectors; Blackwall’s local detector computes similarity and selects candidates.
sequenceConvention: Time flows from top to bottom. Participants are columns. Dashed lines are responses. Conditional messages are optional; they do not mean every request runs every check. Policies are local configuration, not a separate HTTP service.
